title: Effective inseparability

based_on.title: Effective inseparability and some applications in meta-mathematics
based_on.pages: 1010–1031; Definition 1.1, Example 2.2 and selected arguments in §§2.1–2.3, arXiv version 3 (2023-04-09)

summary: Strengthen inseparability to a uniform escape algorithm and characterize the disjoint enumerable pairs that encode every other such pair.
abstract: Two disjoint lists generated by programs may admit no computable rule that assigns every number to the correct side. A stronger obstruction gives an algorithm that, from any proposed disjoint enumerable enlargements of the lists, produces a number missed by both. The familiar pair of programs returning zero or one on their own indices has this property. Moreover, these are exactly the disjoint computably enumerable pairs into which every other disjoint enumerable pair can be translated by one computable map, preserving both membership answers. Uniform self-reference supplies the indices needed for this translation, while a single tagged program lets two recognizers refer to their own indices together.
